result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get attribute values for edges by edge ID. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7497-L7560){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id( edge_attr, edges=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Similar to `get_edge_attrs()` but uses internal edge IDs instead of node pairs. Returns a dictionary keyed by integer edge IDs. Useful when working directly with edge ID references. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Attribute name to extract. [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of edge IDs to query. If `None`, queries all edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping edge IDs to attribute values. Only includes edges that have the attribute set. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} This works like `get_edge_attrs()`, but keys the lookup on edge ID directly rather than searching by source/target -- convenient when IDs are already on hand: ::: {#900db96e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node("A") .add_node("B") .add_node("C") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.5, type="friend") .add_edge("B", "C", weight=2.0, type="colleague") ) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id("weight", edges=edge_ids[:1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 1.5} ``` ::: ::: Omitting `edges=` queries every edge in the graph: ::: {#aa8de4a8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_attrs_by_id("type") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {1: 'friend', 2: 'colleague'} ``` ::: :::
